blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The adult human skeleton comprises 206 bones divided into the axial skeleton (80 bones) and appendicular skeleton (126 bones).
Tendons join skeletal muscles to bones, whereas ligaments connect bone to bone.
Muscular tissue is classified into three types: skeletal (voluntary, striated), smooth (involuntary, non-striated), and cardiac (involuntary, striated).
Major disorders of the skeletal and muscular systems include Osteoporosis, Tetany, Myasthenia Gravis, and Gout.

blocks.content:
The muscular and skeletal system together form the framework of the human body.

The skeletal system provides shape, support, and protection to the body.

The muscular system helps in movement by contracting and relaxing.

Both systems work in coordination to allow locomotion, posture, and balance.

Without muscles, bones cannot move, and without bones, muscles have no support.

This chapter is very important for SSC examinations due to direct factual questions.

The skeletal system consists of bones, cartilage, ligaments, and joints.

It provides structural support to the body.

The skeleton protects vital organs such as the brain, heart, and lungs.

Bones help in movement by acting as levers.

The skeletal system also produces blood cells in bone marrow.

It stores minerals like calcium and phosphorus.

These functions are frequently asked in SSC exams.

Skeletons are classified into three types.

Endoskeleton is found inside the body and is made of bones and cartilage.

Humans have an endoskeleton.

Exoskeleton is found outside the body, as in insects and crustaceans.

Hydrostatic skeleton is found in soft-bodied animals like earthworms.

Spiders use both exoskeleton and hydrostatic pressure for movement.

Classification-based questions are common in SSC.

The human skeleton is divided into two main parts: Axial skeleton and Appendicular skeleton.

The axial skeleton includes skull, vertebral column, ribs, and sternum.

The appendicular skeleton includes limbs and girdles.

The human body has 206 bones.

The skull protects the brain.

The vertebral column protects the spinal cord.

SSC frequently asks number-based questions.

Bones are rigid connective tissues.

They contain calcium salts and collagen fibres.

Bones are of different types: long bones, short bones, flat bones, and irregular bones.

Long bones include femur and humerus.

Flat bones include skull bones.

Bone marrow is of two types: red and yellow.

Red bone marrow produces blood cells.

Yellow bone marrow stores fat.

A joint is a point where two bones meet.

Joints allow movement and flexibility.

Joints are classified into movable, immovable, and slightly movable joints.

Synovial joints are freely movable joints.

Types of synovial joints include hinge, ball and socket, pivot, saddle, and gliding joints.

Knee joint is a hinge joint.

Shoulder joint is a ball and socket joint.

SSC asks examples of joints.

Cartilage is a flexible connective tissue found in nose, ear, and joints.

It provides smooth surfaces for movement.

Ligaments connect bone to bone.

Tendons connect muscle to bone.

Ligaments are elastic while tendons are tough.

Several disorders affect the skeletal system.

Osteoporosis is caused by loss of bone density.

Arthritis causes inflammation of joints.

Gout is caused by deposition of uric acid crystals.

Rickets occurs due to vitamin D deficiency.

These disorders are frequently asked in SSC exams.

The muscular system consists of muscles that help in movement.

Muscles contract and relax to produce movement.

They help in maintaining posture.

Muscles also generate heat.

They assist in circulation and digestion.

Understanding muscle function is important for SSC.

items: Femur (thigh bone) is the longest and strongest bone, while Stapes (middle ear) is the smallest bone in the human body.
Gout occurs due to the accumulation of uric acid crystals in joints, causing severe inflammation.
Tetany is characterized by rapid muscle spasms caused by low calcium (Ca2+) levels in body fluids.
Ligaments connect bone to bone, while tendons connect muscle to bone.

blocks.content:
Muscular tissue is of three types: Skeletal, Smooth, and Cardiac.

Skeletal muscles are voluntary and attached to bones.

Smooth muscles are involuntary and found in internal organs.

Cardiac muscles are involuntary and found only in the heart.

These muscles differ in structure and function.

SSC often asks differences between muscle types.

Muscular disorders affect movement and strength.

Muscular dystrophy is a genetic disorder causing muscle weakness.

Myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune disorder affecting muscle contraction.

Muscle cramps occur due to lack of oxygen or minerals.

These disorders are important for SSC factual questions.

• Human body has 206 bones.

• Femur is the longest bone.

• Stapes is the smallest bone.

• Knee joint is a hinge joint.

• Shoulder joint is a ball and socket joint.

• Ligaments connect bone to bone.

• Tendons connect muscle to bone.

• Red bone marrow forms blood cells.

• Osteoporosis affects bone density.

• Cardiac muscle is involuntary.
